source_text: Fiebatque, ut sicut iudicis aestimatio innocentibus maculabatur addictis, ita generationis status aliorum parentum vindicaretur exemplis. Si enim tramitis, si criminis causa in fecunditatis opere constitisset, omnem fecunditatem condicio ista pollueret.
pass_a_gloss: And it was happening that as the judge's estimation was stained by the innocent condemned, so the status of generation of other parents was vindicated by examples. For if the cause of the path, of the crime, had stood in the work of fecundity, that condition would pollute all fecundity.
pass_b_english: Thus, just as the judge’s reputation would be stained by condemning the innocent, the condition of generation would be vindicated by the examples of other parents. For if the source of the transmission and the guilt lay in the work of reproduction, that condition would pollute all reproduction.

choices.why: For Julian, sin requires rational choice; infants lack usus rationis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
